record.paper_title: Seminar Notes on Open Questions in Iwasawa Theory - SNOQIT I: The Λ[G]-modules of Iwasawa theory II: Units and Kummer theory in Iwasawa extensions
record.original_question: Beyond the class-group modules that arise in classical Iwasawa theory, which other Λ-modules have Property F, and what general hypotheses guarantee that a submodule of a free Λ-module has Property F? The question asks for intrinsic structural criteria, not just isolated examples, so that one can recognize when a projective-limit Λ-module has the same rigidity and decomposition behavior that the paper proves for the standard Iwasawa modules.

evidence.quote: While the property itself can be retained in a simple axiom, it is an important open question, to find out other examples of modules with property F, and possibly some general conditions under which a submodule of a free Λ-module has this property.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $\Lambda = \mathbb{Z}_p[[T]]$ be the Iwasawa algebra. Say that a $\Lambda$-module $M$ has Property F if it satisfies the following axiomatic rigidity/decomposition condition: $M$ embeds as a $\Lambda$-submodule of a free $\Lambda$-module $\Lambda^n$, and every $\Lambda$-linear endomorphism of $M$ extends uniquely to a $\Lambda$-linear endomorphism of the ambient free module compatible with the natural decomposition into isotypic components under any compatible Galois action; equivalently, $M$ shares the structural rigidity established for the standard projective-limit modules of classical Iwasawa theory (such as the inverse limits, along the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-tower, of $p$-parts of ideal class groups of CM fields).

Beyond the class-group modules of classical Iwasawa theory, exhibit further natural examples of $\Lambda$-modules that possess Property F, and formulate intrinsic structural hypotheses on a $\Lambda$-submodule $M \subseteq \Lambda^n$ of a free $\Lambda$-module that are sufficient to guarantee that $M$ has Property F.
artifact.status_search_result: No subsequent literature was located that resolves the question of intrinsic structural criteria characterizing $\Lambda$-modules with Property F or that provides general hypotheses ensuring a submodule of a free $\Lambda$-module has Property F. The problem is posed as an open axiomatic-classification question and no published resolution was found in the available search results.

status_evidence.title: The T and T* components of Λ-modules and Leopoldt's conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Work by Mihailescu on structural decomposition of Λ[Gal(K/Q)]-modules arising in Iwasawa theory; addresses related rigidity but not a general Property F criterion.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related work on Λ-module structure exists but does not give a general Property F characterization.

status_evidence.title: Iwasawa theory - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Standard structure theory describes finitely generated torsion Λ-modules up to pseudo-isomorphism but does not address the axiomatic Property F.
status_evidence.claim: Standard Iwasawa structure theory does not resolve the Property F question.
